title: Research 10 recommended Girona places and save cited source data.
acceptance: The task performs web research before creating or editing the travel-guide page files
docs/girona-research.json exists and contains exactly 10 recommended places to visit in Girona
Each place includes name, category, short description, openingHours, officialUrl, sourceUrl, sourceTitle, and retrievedDate fields
Opening hours are included when available from checked sources, and uncertain hours are explicitly marked as not available instead of invented
The selected places cover a useful mix of landmarks, historic streets, museums, viewpoints, bridges, parks, markets, or food-related stops
At least 7 of the 10 entries use official attraction, official tourism, municipal, museum, or public tourism body sources

title: Create the static Girona travel-guide HTML shell in webs/travel.html.
acceptance: webs/travel.html exists and identifies the page as a mini travel guide for Girona
The page links to travel.css and travel.js and uses no external dependencies
The first viewport includes the Girona title, a short practical intro, search input, category filter controls, and a visible start of the card grid
The page includes semantic regions for header, controls, card grid, empty state, and sources
The page includes a noscript message explaining that cards and filters need JavaScript
The markup provides stable ids or data hooks needed by travel.js

title: Style the responsive card-based travel guide in webs/travel.css.
acceptance: webs/travel.css creates a responsive card grid that works on mobile, tablet, and desktop widths
Search and category controls are visible, compact, and usable without overlapping other content
Cards clearly separate place name, category, description, opening hours, official link, and citation link
The layout avoids oversized marketing-style hero sections and keeps guide content visible in the first viewport
Focus-visible, hover, active, and selected states are defined for interactive controls and links
The page has no horizontal overflow or clipped text at common mobile widths

title: Render researched places as cards from structured data in webs/travel.js.
acceptance: webs/travel.js loads or defines the 10 researched places using the same fields saved in docs/girona-research.json
The script renders exactly 10 place cards on initial load
Each rendered card shows name, category, short description, opening hours or an explicit unavailable-hours message, official link when available, and source citation link
External links use safe new-tab attributes when opening in a new tab
The script renders a sources section listing all distinct sources used by the card data
The app handles missing optional officialUrl values without breaking card rendering

title: Implement search and category filtering in webs/travel.js.
acceptance: The search input filters cards by place name, category, description, and opening-hours text
Category controls filter cards by category
Search and category filters work together rather than replacing each other
An empty-state message appears when no cards match the active filters
A clear or all-categories control restores the full 10-card list
Filtering updates visible result counts or equivalent status text for user feedback

title: Add traveler-focused content polish and citation quality checks.
acceptance: Descriptions are concise, original summaries suitable for visitors and not copied from source pages
Every card has a useful category label and practical opening-hours text
Every card has either an official link or a clearly relevant public tourism source link
The sources section is readable and includes retrieval dates
The page clearly distinguishes official links from citation/source links
No place entry contains placeholder text, fake URLs, or invented hours

title: Verify responsive behavior, accessibility, and static-site quality.
acceptance: webs/travel.html can be opened through a simple local server without build steps
The browser console has no errors during initial load, search, filtering, and link interaction
Keyboard users can reach search, filters, cards, and links in a logical order
Interactive controls have accessible names and visible focus indicators
The card grid remains readable at desktop and mobile viewport widths
The implementation is organized into readable HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with no external dependencies
